The Kokatha, also known as the Kokatha Mula, are an Aboriginal Australian people of South Australia, in the arid country north of the Eyre Peninsula and west of Lake Torrens. The map shows them from 1600 to 1815. Their language is close to, or a dialect of, the Western Desert language of the Western Desert cultural bloc.

Their neighbours were the Wirangu to the south, the Arabana to the east and the Antakirinja to the north. After 1947 much of their country became the Woomera rocket range, and in the 1950s British atomic tests further west, the Maralinga tests, closed off more of the desert. The huge Olympic Dam copper and uranium mine at Roxby Downs opened on their land in 1988. In 2014 a court recognised Kokatha native title over a large area.
